title: Incorrect error message if vault is corrupt
line: Unlocking a CryFS vault with a damaged configuration file no longer just says the password is wrong, and the error now has a Details button with CryFS's own message.
explanation: CryFS exits with code 11 both when the password is wrong and when cryfs.config can't be decrypted or parsed (e.g. it's truncated). The CryFS backend mapped that code to 'You entered the wrong password' and dropped CryFS's output, so a corrupt vault looked like a typo and the real cause was only in the logs. The message now names both causes and passes CryFS's stdout/stderr, so the dialog's Details button shows the actual error (e.g. 'Error deserializing outer configuration').

commits.message:
cryfs: don't blame the password when the vault config can't be read

CryFS uses the same exit code for a wrong password and for a damaged or
unreadable configuration file, so a corrupt vault told the user that the
password was wrong. Mention both causes and show the CryFS output too.

BUG: 427108

patches.diff:
From acd81fd3d9918dc8a9f57096ce3d36cfd6bab1cd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 03:59:33 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] cryfs: don't blame the password when the vault config can't
 be read

CryFS uses the same exit code for a wrong password and for a damaged or
unreadable configuration file, so a corrupt vault told the user that the
password was wrong. Mention both causes and show the CryFS output too.

BUG: 427108
---
 kded/engine/backends/cryfs/cryfsbackend.cpp | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/kded/engine/backends/cryfs/cryfsbackend.cpp b/kded/engine/backends/cryfs/cryfsbackend.cpp
index f425eb3..a1c2020 100644
--- a/kded/engine/backends/cryfs/cryfsbackend.cpp
+++ b/kded/engine/backends/cryfs/cryfsbackend.cpp
@@ -155,7 +155,8 @@ FutureResult<> CryFsBackend::mount(const Device &device, const MountPoint &mount
 
             exitCode == ExitCode::WrongPassword ?
                 Result<>::error(Error::BackendError,
-                                i18n("You entered the wrong password")) :
+                                i18n("You entered the wrong password, or the vault's configuration file is damaged"),
+                                out, err) :
 
             exitCode == ExitCode::TooNewFilesystemFormat ?
                 Result<>::error(Error::BackendError,
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Corrupt CryFS vault (cryfs.config truncated), correct password: 'You entered the wrong password'
Same vault: 'You entered the wrong password, or the vault's configuration file is damaged', with a Details button
Before: no Details button, CryFS's own error is not shown anywhere in the UI
Details shows CryFS's output: 'Error deserializing outer configuration … Failed to decrypt the config file'

review.text: Updating CryFsBackend::mount()'s ExitCode::WrongPassword message to mention both a wrong password and a damaged configuration file while passing CryFS's stdout/stderr as details accurately reflects CryFS's ambiguous exit code 11. This avoids misleading users with corrupt vaults, surfaces CryFS's real deserialization error via the Details button without brittle stderr parsing or password exposure, and is cleanly verified on both corrupt and healthy CryFS vaults.
